phase: P09 — Windows companion build and Rust safety execution
summary: The Rust safety core type-checks, formats and lints cleanly, but its 25 tests have never executed because no C++ linker is installed. This is the same blocker native/companion/README.md has always declared, now measured rather than asserted.

observed.note: Compiles to object code. Proves the source is valid Rust; proves nothing about behaviour.

observed.error: linking with `link.exe` failed: exit code: 1 — link: missing operand after '\377\376'
observed.diagnosis: The `link.exe` found on PATH is GNU coreutils `link` from Git Bash (/usr/bin/link), not the MSVC linker. Its error text ('Try link --help') is the coreutils message. rustc invoked it with MSVC linker arguments, which it cannot parse. No Visual Studio installation exists under either Program Files path.
observed.note: This is the exact failure native/companion/README.md predicted.

mostSignificant.name: mac_matches_typescript_golden_vectors
mostSignificant.why: It asserts the SAME golden HMAC-SHA-256 table as the TypeScript half in src/lib/__tests__/companion-client.test.ts. The TypeScript side runs and passes today. Until the Rust side executes, wire-format agreement between the two halves is assumed, not verified — and a silent disagreement would mean the host rejects every signed envelope the page produces.

whatThisDoesNotProve: That the Rust safety core behaves correctly. Compiling is not running.
That protected-input refusal, allowlist enforcement, path canonicalisation, replay rejection or emergency stop work at all.
That the companion can be built, signed, installed or launched.
Any of the 18 items on the README runtime checklist, all of which remain unticked.

unblockedBy.action: Install a C++ linker, then run `cargo test -p caera-companion-safety`.

options.what: Visual Studio Build Tools with the 'Desktop development with C++' workload
options.note: Matches the existing default toolchain (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc); nothing else changes.
Lighter, but builds a GNU-ABI binary. Acceptable for EXECUTING the safety-core tests; the shipped companion should still be built with MSVC to match the platform it targets.

unblockedBy.alsoNote: Git Bash's /usr/bin/link shadows the MSVC linker on PATH in this shell. After installing MSVC tools, run cargo from a Developer Command Prompt or ensure the MSVC bin directory precedes /usr/bin.

honestClassification: The 27 requirements covering Desktop Companion Foundation, Windows Process/Application/Window Control, scoped input and part of Accessibility remain EXTERNALLY BLOCKED / ONE HUMAN ACTION AWAY. `cargo check` passing does not move any of them, and this file exists so that it cannot be mistaken for progress.
